title: Bioactive compound C498-0670 alleviates LPS-induced sepsis via JAK/STAT and NFkappaB signaling pathways.
authors: Xu, Jing; Zhang, Xinxin; Zhou, Mingming; Lu, Peizhe; Xu, Yuting; Wu, Lihong; Zhang, Qianyue; Wu, Zhihua; Xu, Xiaoyu; Shi, Pengfei; Wei, Qingda; Li, Xiaoyu; Song, Qiaoling
one_liner_zh: 该文研究小分子化合物C498-0670抑制JAK/STAT和NFkappaB信号通路以缓解脓毒症，虽涉及分子对接但对象为蛋白-小分子，非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: The JAK/STAT and NFkappaB signaling pathways are two major inflammatory signaling pathways that are usually activated simultaneously in the body's inflammatory response to bacterial or viral infections. Hyperactivation of these two prominent signaling pathways is associated with various immune-related diseases and mortality, pointing to an urgent need for drug development targeting JAK/STAT and/or NFkappaB signaling. In this study, we screened 18,840 compounds using our well-established dual STAT-NFkappaB driven luciferase reporter based high-throughput screening system and identified a bioactive compound C498-0670, which inhibits both JAK/STAT and NFkappaB signaling. C498-0670 inhibits the activation of STATs and p-IKKalpha/beta in both the immortalized cell lines and primary peritoneal macrophages, while suppressing the expression of LPS-induced inflammatory mediators in vitro. In addition, the overall anti-inflammatory effects of C498-0670 were investigated using transcriptome sequencing and bioinformatics approaches. C498-0670 was predicted to alleviate sepsis/septic shock by disease/function analysis using IPA software, which was further verified in the LPS-induced mouse sepsis model in vivo. C498 reduced LPS-induced liver and kidney damage, myeloid cell infiltration, and pro-inflammatory cytokine and chemokine production in vivo. Furthermore, the SPR-HPLC-MS-based target fishing approach was used to identify the putative drug targets, and the high affinities of JAK2 (JAK/STAT signaling), NFKBIA (NFkappaB signaling), and IL-1beta, NLRP1b (inflammasome signaling) for C498-0670 were verified by molecular docking approach. These results suggest that C498-0670 can be used as a dual-target inhibitor of JAK/STAT and NFkappaB signaling pathways for the treatment of various inflammatory diseases, especially septic shock.
abstract_zh: JAK/STAT和NFkappaB信号通路是两条主要的炎症信号通路，通常在机体对细菌或病毒感染的炎症反应中同时被激活。这两条显著信号通路的过度激活与多种免疫相关疾病及死亡率相关，表明迫切需要开发靶向JAK/STAT和/或NFkappaB信号的药物。在本研究中，我们利用已建立的基于双STAT-NFkappaB驱动的荧光素酶报告基因的高通量筛选系统，筛选了18,840种化合物，并鉴定出一种生物活性化合物C498-0670，该化合物同时抑制JAK/STAT和NFkappaB信号。C498-0670在永生化细胞系和原代腹腔巨噬细胞中抑制STATs和p-IKKalpha/beta的激活，同时在体外抑制LPS诱导的炎症介质表达。此外，通过转录组测序和生物信息学方法研究了C498-0670的整体抗炎效果。使用IPA软件进行疾病/功能分析预测C498-0670可缓解脓毒症/脓毒性休克，并在体内LPS诱导的小鼠脓毒症模型中进一步验证。C498在体内减少LPS诱导的肝脏和肾脏损伤、髓系细胞浸润以及促炎细胞因子和趋化因子的产生。此外，采用基于SPR-HPLC-MS的靶点钓取方法鉴定推定药物靶点，并通过分子对接方法验证了JAK2（JAK/STAT信号）、NFKBIA（NFkappaB信号）以及IL-1beta、NLRP1b（炎症小体信号）对C498-0670的高亲和力。这些结果表明，C498-0670可作为JAK/STAT和NFkappaB信号通路的双靶点抑制剂，用于治疗多种炎症性疾病，尤其是脓毒性休克。
